findings: 2026-11-05: drafted for Mathematics 11 Unit 7 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.
Book correction: In the second line of the proof the left side is misprinted as {}^{n}C_{n-,} (a broken subscript). It should read {}^{n}C_{n-r} = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!\,(n-n+r)!}

Book correction: Example 12(ii): the conclusion prints "If repetition of characters is not allowed". Part (ii) is the case where repetition is allowed; it should read: Hence, 36^{6} passwords can be generated by using the 26 alphabets and 10 digits, if repetition of characters is allowed.
